requirements.text: The ESA sample(s) submitted for type approval shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark and the type designation.

An approval mark as described in paragraph 5.3. shall be affixed to every ESA conforming to a type approved under this Regulation, except that no marking is required for electrical/electronic systems built into vehicles which are approved as units.

A vehicle and its electrical/electronic system(s) or ESA(s) shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
A vehicle shall be tested for radiated emissions and for immunity to radiated disturbances for vehicle type approval.
ESA(s) shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions and for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.
The electromagnetic radiation generated by the vehicle representative of its type shall be measured using the method described in Annex 4.

Where vehicle broadband radiation measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the vehicle broadband emissions shall not exceed 32 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band.

Where vehicle broadband radiation measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the vehicle broadband emissions shall not exceed 32 to 43 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz.

Where vehicle broadband radiation measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the vehicle broadband emissions shall not exceed 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band.

Where vehicle broadband radiation measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the vehicle broadband emissions shall not exceed 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 3 to this Regulation.

Where vehicle broadband radiation measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the vehicle broadband emissions shall not exceed the constant limit of 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the vehicle representative of its type, the measured broadband values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the vehicle broadband type approval limits.
The narrowband electromagnetic radiation generated by the vehicle representative of its type shall be measured using the method described in Annex 5.

The vehicle narrowband type approval limit shall be 28 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 230 MHz frequency band if measurements are made using the method described in Annex 5 using a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m.

The vehicle narrowband type approval limit shall be 35 dB microvolts/m in the 230 to 1,000 MHz frequency band if measurements are made using the method described in Annex 5 using a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m.

The vehicle narrowband type approval limit shall be 38 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 230 MHz frequency band if measurements are made using the method described in Annex 5 using a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m.

The vehicle narrowband type approval limit shall be 45 dB microvolts/m in the 230 to 1,000 MHz frequency band if measurements are made using the method described in Annex 5 using a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m.
On the vehicle representative of its type, the measured narrowband values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the vehicle narrowband type approval limit.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the vehicle representative of its type shall be tested by the method described in Annex 6.

If vehicle immunity tests are made using the method described in Annex 6 in accordance with ISO 11451-2, the field strength shall be 30 volts/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band and a minimum of 25 volts/m over the whole 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.

If vehicle immunity tests are made using the method described in Annex 6 in accordance with ISO 11451-2, the field strength shall be 10 volts/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band and a minimum of 8 volts/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.

If vehicle immunity tests are made using the method described in Annex 6 in accordance with ISO 11451-4 BCI, the current shall be 60 mA in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band and a minimum of 50 mA over the whole 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.

The vehicle representative of its type shall show no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions", according to paragraph 2.1. of Annex 6, during the tests performed in accordance with Annex 6.
The broadband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband type approval limit shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband type approval limit shall be 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.
Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband type approval limit shall remain constant at 63 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
The narrowband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 8.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband type approval limit shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, as shown in Appendix 7.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband type approval limit shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz, as shown in Appendix 7.
Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband type approval limit shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured narrowband value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.

The emission of transient conducted disturbances on 12/24 V supply lines of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 for the levels given in Table 1.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9.

The ESA representative of its type shall withstand, in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, a stripline test level of 60 V/m over 20 to 400 MHz when tested by the method described in Annex 9.

The ESA representative of its type shall withstand, in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, a TEM cell test level of 75 V/m over 20 to 200 MHz when tested by the method described in Annex 9.

The ESA representative of its type shall withstand, in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, a BCI test level of 60 mA over 20 to 400 MHz when tested by the method described in Annex 9.

The ESA representative of its type shall withstand, in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, an ALSE test level of 30 V/m over 80 to 2,000 MHz and 10 V/m over 2,000 to 6,000 MHz when tested by the method described in Annex 9.

The ESA representative of its type shall withstand, in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, a reverberation chamber test level of 21 V/m over LUF to 2,000 MHz and 7 V/m over 2,000 to 6,000 MHz when tested by the method described in Annex 9.

The ESA representative of its type shall withstand, over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, a minimum stripline test level of 50 V/m over 20 to 400 MHz when tested by the method described in Annex 9.

The ESA representative of its type shall withstand, over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, a minimum TEM cell test level of 62,5 V/m over 20 to 200 MHz when tested by the method described in Annex 9.
The ESA representative of its type shall withstand, over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, a minimum BCI test level of 50 mA over 20 to 400 MHz when tested by the method described in Annex 9.

The ESA representative of its type shall withstand, over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, a minimum ALSE test level of 25 V/m over 80 to 2,000 MHz and 8 V/m over 2,000 to 6,000 MHz when tested by the method described in Annex 9.

The ESA representative of its type shall withstand, over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, a minimum reverberation chamber test level of 18 V/m over LUF to 2,000 MHz and 6 V/m over 2,000 to 6,000 MHz when tested by the method described in Annex 9.
The ESA representative of its type shall show no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions" during the tests performed in accordance with Annex 9.

The ESA representative of its type shall be immune to transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines when tested according to ISO 16750-2 for starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.

For ESAs that could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started with a 12V/24V starter motor, the ESA shall meet, for the starting profile at immunity test level II for 12 V and 24 V systems with 10 pulses, functional status classification B for immunity related functions where the ESA shall be operational during engine start phases, according to ISO 16750-1.

For ESAs that could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started with a 12V/24V starter motor, the ESA shall meet, for the starting profile at immunity test level II for 12 V and 24 V systems with 10 pulses, functional status classification C for immunity related functions where the ESA is not required to be operational during engine start phases, according to ISO 16750-1.

For ESAs that could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started with a 12V/24V starter motor, the ESA shall meet, for the starting profile at immunity test level II for 12 V and 24 V systems with 10 pulses, functional status classification D for functions not related to immunity related functions, according to ISO 16750-1.

The ESA shall meet FPSC III as in ISO 7637-1 for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions when subjected to test pulse 1 at -75 V for 12 V systems and -450 V for 24 V systems with 500 pulses.

The ESA shall meet FPSC I as in ISO 7637-1 for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions when subjected to test pulse 2a at +37 V for 12 V systems and +37 V for 24 V systems with 500 pulses.

The ESA shall meet FPSC II as in ISO 7637-1 for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions when subjected to test pulse 2b at +10 V for 12 V systems and +20 V for 24 V systems with 10 pulses.

The ESA shall meet FPSC I as in ISO 7637-1 for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions when subjected to test pulse 3a at -112 V for 12 V systems and -150 V for 24 V systems for a test duration of 1 h.

The ESA shall meet FPSC I as in ISO 7637-1 for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions when subjected to test pulse 3b at +75 V for 12 V systems and +150 V for 24 V systems for a test duration of 1 h.
The vehicle narrowband radiated emission, at an antenna-vehicle separation of 10 m, shall not exceed the limit E = 28 dBµV/m in the frequency range 30-230 MHz, measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth.
The vehicle narrowband radiated emission, at an antenna-vehicle separation of 10 m, shall not exceed the limit E = 35 dBµV/m in the frequency range 230-1,000 MHz, measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth.

The test of broadband emissions generated by electrical or electronic systems fitted to the vehicle (e.g. ignition system or electric motors) shall be performed according to CISPR 12, if not otherwise stated in Annex 4.
During the broadband emission test of a vehicle in configuration other than "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the engine shall be in operation according to CISPR 12.

For a vehicle with an electric propulsion motor or hybrid propulsion system, if the operating mode defined in CISPR 12 (i.e. 40 km/h) does not activate all traction motors or auxiliary battery charging engines, the vehicle shall be operated in an alternative, steady state operating mode agreed between the Technical Service and vehicle manufacturer.
The vehicle shall be tested for narrowband electromagnetic emissions emanating from microprocessor-based systems or other narrowband sources according to CISPR 12, unless otherwise stated in Annex 5.
During the narrowband emission test, the vehicle ignition switch shall be switched on.
During the narrowband emission test, the vehicle engine shall not be operating.
During the narrowband emission test, the vehicle's electronic systems shall all be in normal operating mode with the vehicle stationary.

The vehicle electronic systems shall demonstrate immunity when the vehicle is subjected to electromagnetic fields as described in Annex 6, tested according to ISO 11451-2 in an ALSE unless otherwise stated in Annex 6.
For vehicles not considered as "large vehicles", the vehicle shall be subjected to front irradiation, with rear irradiation as specified in paragraph 5.1.3 of Annex 6.

For "large vehicles", the vehicle shall be subjected to front irradiation and to additional antenna positions chosen by the manufacturer in conjunction with the Type-Approval Authority after considering the distribution of electronic systems with immunity related functions and the layout of any wiring harness.
The vehicle immunity tests shall be performed with the levels defined in paragraph 6.4.2.1. of this Regulation.
For REESS charging mode, only the electronic systems and wiring harnesses required for charging mode shall be considered for antenna positions.

Where the vehicle immunity test is alternatively performed in an outdoor test site (OTS) according to ISO 11451-2, a vehicle not considered as a "large vehicle" shall be tested with front irradiation, with rear irradiation as specified in paragraph 5.1.3.

Where the vehicle immunity test is alternatively performed in an outdoor test site (OTS) according to ISO 11451-2, the vehicle shall be tested with levels defined in paragraph 6.4.2.1. of this Regulation.
For REESS charging mode, only the electronic systems and wiring harnesses required for charging mode shall be considered for antenna positions in the alternative outdoor test site test.
The vehicle in configuration other than "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" shall be in an unladen condition except for necessary test equipment during the immunity test.
During the immunity test, the engine shall normally turn the driving wheels at a steady speed of 50 km/h if there is no technical reason due to the vehicle to define a different condition.

In the "50 km/h mode" immunity test with vehicle speed 50 km/h ±20 per cent (vehicle driving the rollers), the vehicle shall not exhibit a speed variation greater than ±10 per cent of the nominal speed.

If the vehicle is equipped with a cruise control system, it shall be used to maintain the required constant vehicle speed in the "50 km/h mode" immunity test and shall be maintained without any deactivation.
In case of automatic gearbox, the vehicle in the "50 km/h mode" immunity test shall not exhibit a change of gear ratio inducing a speed variation greater than ±10 per cent of the nominal speed.
With dipped beams ON (manual mode) in the "50 km/h mode" immunity test, the front and rear lighting shall not switch OFF.
With specific warning OFF in the "50 km/h mode" immunity test, the specific warning (e.g. rotating/flashing light, signalling bar, siren) shall not switch ON.
With the cluster operating in normal mode in the "50 km/h mode" immunity test, the cluster shall not show an unexpected warning or an inconsistent variation of the odometer.
In the "50 km/h mode" immunity test, the rear view system shall not exhibit unexpected movement of the rear view mirror or loss or freezing of the display (CMS).
With the front wiper ON (manual mode) at maximum speed in the "50 km/h mode" immunity test, the front wiper shall not come to a complete stop.
With the direction indicator on the driver's side ON in the "50 km/h mode" immunity test, the direction indicator shall not exhibit a frequency change lower than 0.75 Hz or greater than 2.25 Hz.

With the direction indicator on the driver's side ON in the "50 km/h mode" immunity test, the direction indicator shall not exhibit a duty cycle change lower than 25 per cent or greater than 75 per cent.
With adjustable suspension in normal position in the "50 km/h mode" immunity test, the suspension shall not exhibit unexpected significant variation.
With the driver's seat and steering wheel in medium position in the "50 km/h mode" immunity test, they shall not exhibit unexpected variation greater than 10 per cent of total range.
With the alarm unset in the "50 km/h mode" immunity test, there shall be no unexpected activation of the alarm.
With the horn OFF in the "50 km/h mode" immunity test, there shall be no unexpected activation of the horn.

With airbag and safety restraint systems operational with inhibited passenger airbag if this function exists in the "50 km/h mode" immunity test, there shall be no unexpected activation of the airbag and safety restraint systems.
With automatic doors closed in the "50 km/h mode" immunity test, there shall be no unexpected opening of the doors.
With the adjustable endurance brake lever in normal position in the "50 km/h mode" immunity test, there shall be no unexpected activation of the endurance brake.
With the brake pedal not depressed in the "50 km/h mode" immunity test, there shall be no unexpected activation of the brake and no unexpected activation of the stop lights.
ADS shall be operational in the "50 km/h mode" immunity test and shall not remain in a failure safe mode or expected failure operational mode.
During the immunity test, all other systems which affect the driver's control of the vehicle shall be (on) as in normal operation of the vehicle.
The vehicle in configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" shall be in an unladen condition except for necessary test equipment during the immunity test.
The vehicle in "REESS charging mode" shall not set itself in motion during the vehicle immunity tests.
The vehicle in "REESS charging mode" shall not exhibit an unexpected release of the parking brake during the vehicle immunity tests.
The vehicle with automatic transmission in "REESS charging mode" shall not exhibit a loss of the Parking position during the vehicle immunity tests.
The vehicle shall be exposed to electromagnetic radiation in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges in vertical polarization.

The test signal modulation for the vehicle immunity test shall be AM (amplitude modulation), with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and vehicle manufacturer.

The test signal modulation for the vehicle immunity test shall be PM2 (pulse modulation type 2), Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs in the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and vehicle manufacturer.

The test signal modulation for the vehicle immunity test shall be PM3 (pulse modulation type 3), Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs in the 380 to 2,700 MHz and the 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and vehicle manufacturer.
The ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
For ESA other than involved in "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in Clause 6.4 of CISPR 25.
The ESA narrowband electromagnetic emissions test shall be performed according to CISPR 25, if not otherwise stated in Annex 8.
The ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load, during the narrowband electromagnetic emissions tests.
The ESA narrowband electromagnetic emissions test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in paragraph 6.4. of CISPR 25.

The ESA shall comply with the requirements of any combination of the absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2, TEM cell testing according to ISO 11452-3, bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4, stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5 and reverberation chamber test according to ISO 11452-11, at the manufacturer's discretion, provided that the results cover the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of Annex 9, with frequency range and general test conditions based on ISO 11452-1.
The test conditions for the ESA immunity tests shall be according to ISO 11452-1.
The ESA under test shall be switched on and shall be stimulated to be in normal operation condition.
The ESA under test shall be arranged as defined in Annex 9 unless individual test methods dictate otherwise.

If the ESA under test consists of more than one unit and the wiring harnesses as intended for use in the vehicle are not available as interconnecting cables, the length between the electronic control unit and the AN shall be as defined in the standard.
The ESA shall be tested for immunity in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range with frequency steps according to ISO 11452-1.

The test signal modulation for the ESA immunity test shall be AM (amplitude modulation), with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

The test signal modulation for the ESA immunity test shall be PM2 (pulse modulation type 2), Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs in the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

The test signal modulation for the ESA immunity test shall be PM3 (pulse modulation type 3), Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs in the 380 to 2,700 MHz and the 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.
The frequency step size and dwell time for the ESA immunity test shall be chosen according to ISO 11452-1.
The ESA shall meet the immunity requirements of Annex 9 throughout the frequency range 20 to 6,000 MHz, at the intervals specified in ISO 11452-1.
The ESA shall be immune to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply as tested according to Annex 10.
The ESA shall limit conducted transients from the ESA to the vehicle power supply as tested according to Annex 10.

An international approval mark conforming to the model described in Annex 2 shall be affixed, conspicuously and in a readily accessible place specified on the approval form, to every vehicle conforming to a vehicle type approved under UN Regulation No. 175.

If the vehicle conforms to a vehicle type approved under one or more other Regulations annexed to the Agreement in the country which has granted approval under UN Regulation No. 175, the Regulation and approval numbers and the additional symbols shall be placed in vertical columns to the right of the approval mark symbol, which need not be repeated.
The approval mark shall be clearly legible and be indelible.
The approval mark shall be placed close to or on the vehicle data plate.

The ACPE performance requirements shall be met by a vehicle with no trailer coupled, with a mass between maximum mass and mass in running order, and whose powertrain management system is properly operational.

The ACPE shall be able to limit unintended acceleration of the vehicle when an accelerator control misapplication by the driver has been detected at least when an obstacle exists in front of the vehicle when the driving direction is selected to be forward.

The ACPE shall be able to limit unintended acceleration of the vehicle when an accelerator control misapplication by the driver has been detected at least when an obstacle exists behind the vehicle when the driving direction is selected to be rearwards.

The ACPE shall regard as an accelerator control misapplication an accelerator control application having a velocity of at least 400 per cent per second over a travel distance of at least 70 per cent of the total travel distance of the accelerator control, and reaching a maximum position of the accelerator control of at least 90 per cent with that velocity.
The ACPE shall control acceleration when the vehicle is accelerated from standstill.
If the ACPE is not ready to perform an intervention 6 seconds after the initiation of the vehicle powertrain, information of this status shall be indicated to the driver.
The information that the ACPE is not ready to perform an intervention shall exist until the system has been successfully initialised.

The ACPE shall limit vehicle acceleration in order to prevent or mitigate a collision with an obstacle located between 1.0 m and 1.5 m in front of or behind the vehicle, in the vehicle path, at the time the accelerator control is applied, for a vehicle with no trailer coupled, with a mass between maximum mass and mass in running order and whose powertrain management system is properly operational, provided that: (a) vehicle external influences allow for the required acceleration inhibition (the road is flat, horizontal and dry affording good adhesion, and the weather conditions do not affect the performance of the vehicle, e.g. no storm, not below 0°C); (b) the vehicle state itself allows for the required acceleration inhibition (e.g. tyres in an appropriate state and properly inflated, brakes if intended to be used properly operational, no severe uneven load distribution, no trailer coupled and mass between maximum mass and mass in running order, powertrain management system properly operational); (c) there are no external influences affecting the physical sensing capabilities (ambient illumination at least 1000 Lux and no extreme blinding of the sensors, target vehicle not extreme with regard to Radar Cross Section (RCS) or shape/silhouette, e.g. below fifth percentile of RCS of all M1 vehicles, no significant weather conditions affecting the sensing capabilities such as heavy rain, dense fog, snow, dirt, and no overhead obstructions close to the vehicle); and (d) the situation is unambiguous (the obstacle is stationary, unobstructed and clearly separated from other objects in the driving direction, the lateral offset between the centreline of the obstacle and the centreline of the vehicle is not more than 0.2 m, the direction of travel is straight with no curve and the vehicle is not turning at an intersection and following its lane, and the obstacle is a vehicle of category M1 or a wall like structure with a width of at least 2.0 m and a height of at least 1.0 m).

When conditions deviate from those listed for the ACPE acceleration limitation performance, the ACPE shall not deactivate or unreasonably switch the control strategy, as demonstrated in accordance with Annex 3.

In the case that a collision is not prevented by the ACPE, the collision speed shall be no greater than 8 km/h higher than the vehicle speed at the point where the triggering conditions specified in paragraph 5.1.2. are met.

In the case that a collision is not prevented by the ACPE, the collision speed shall not be greater than 70% of that speed the vehicle would have had in the same position and under the same circumstances but without any ACPE intervention.

For vehicles that do not exceed 8 km/h without ACPE in the test scenarios but for which a speed reduction of 30 per cent cannot be achieved due to a low engine power to test mass ratio, the ACPE speed reduction shall be of at least 15 per cent.

During any ACPE intervention, the vehicle acceleration shall continue to be limited by the ACPE, with the intervention only allowed to end when the obstacle is no longer detected or the driver has interrupted the function.

The effectiveness of the ACPE shall not be adversely affected by magnetic or electrical fields, demonstrated by fulfilling the technical requirements and respecting the transitional provisions of the 06 or later series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 10.
The ACPE shall show conformity with the safety aspects of electronic control systems by meeting the requirements of Annex 3.
The ACPE shall inform the driver of its intervention in accordance with paragraph 5.4.2.
The ACPE shall provide a means for the driver to interrupt its intervention.
The interruption of the ACPE intervention shall be started by any intentional action which indicates that the driver has recognised the situation.
In the case of interruption of the ACPE intervention by maintaining the accelerator control application, there shall be no rapid increase of acceleration.

The ACPE performance requirements shall be verified using the test procedure as described in section 6, for a vehicle with no trailer coupled, with a mass between maximum mass and mass in running order, and whose powertrain management system is properly operational.

When a vehicle is equipped with a means to manually deactivate the ACPE, the ACPE shall be automatically reinstated at the initiation of any new engine start (or run cycle, as relevant), except when a new engine start (or run cycle, as relevant) is performed automatically, e.g., the operation of a stop/start system.
When a vehicle is equipped with a means to manually deactivate the ACPE, a deactivation warning shall be given at least at the time of deactivation.
A failure warning shall be given to the driver when there is a failure in the ACPE that prevents the requirements of this Regulation being met.
The ACPE failure warning shall be as specified in paragraph 5.4.3.
There shall not be an appreciable time interval between each ACPE self-check.

There shall not be a delay in illuminating the ACPE failure warning signal in the case of an electrically detectable failure, except that if the vehicle speed is greater than 10 km/h at the time a failure is detected, the warning signal may be suppressed until the next time the vehicle speed is below 10 km/h.

A failure warning shall be given to the driver in the case of a detected non-electrical ACPE failure condition (e.g. sensor blindness or sensor misalignment) unless a deactivation warning is given as per paragraph 5.2.3.1.3.
The ACPE optical warning signals shall be visible even by daylight.
The satisfactory condition of the ACPE optical warning signals shall be easily verifiable by the driver from the driver's seat.

Each ACPE optical warning signal, except warning signals shown in a common space, shall be activated either when the engine start (or run, as relevant) switch is turned to the "on" (run) position or when the engine start (or run, as relevant) switch is in a position between the "on" (run) and "start" position that is designated by the manufacturer as a check position (initial system (power-on)).
The ACPE intervention warning shall be given by an optical signal.

In addition to the optical intervention warning signal, a haptic or acoustic signal shall be provided to the driver, unless such a signal is already being provided by another vehicle system comprising an object detection capability (e.g. parking distance warning).
The ACPE failure warning shall be given by a constant yellow optical signal.
At a Periodic Technical Inspection, it shall be possible to confirm the correct operational status of the ACPE by a visible observation of the failure warning signal status.

Following a "power-ON" and any bulb check, the ACPE failure warning signal shall remain illuminated if any failure was present at the end of the previous engine start (or run, as relevant) cycle, unless this failure is detected to be no longer present.

The ACPE shall be provided with means to protect against simple unauthorised modification of the operation of the failure warning signal, or alternatively with a secondary means of checking the correct operational status of the ACPE.
The ACPE shall meet the test requirements when tested on a flat, dry, concrete or asphalt road affording good adhesion.
The ACPE shall meet the test requirements at an ambient temperature between 0°C and 45°C.
The vehicle shall meet the ACPE requirements when tested at the minimum mass (mass in running order with an additional mass of maximum 125 kg).

The vehicle shall meet the ACPE requirements when tested at any other mass up to the technically permissible maximum laden mass as defined by the manufacturer, where the technical service deems this justified.
The ACPE shall meet the accelerator control misapplication test with a lateral offset between the centreline of the target and the centreline of the vehicle of between 0.0 m and 0.2 m.

The ACPE shall meet the accelerator control misapplication test performed with and without an expected ACPE intervention, both in a forward and rearward direction, and at least with the vehicle situated 1.0 m (+0.1 m tolerance) and 1.5 m (-0.1 m tolerance) from the target position at the start of the test, as detailed in Table 1.

The special requirements for documentation, fault strategy and verification of Annex 3 shall apply to the Complex Electronic Vehicle Control Systems and to the safety related functions identified in this Regulation which are controlled by electronic system(s).
"The System" shall respect, under non-fault and fault conditions, all the appropriate performance requirements specified elsewhere in this Regulation.
"The System" shall be designed to operate in such a way that it does not induce safety critical risks.

The manufacturer shall provide a documentation package which gives access to the basic design of "The System" and the means by which it is linked to other vehicle systems or by which it directly controls output variables.
The documentation shall explain the function(s) of "The System" and the safety concept, as laid down by the manufacturer.
The documentation shall be brief, yet provide evidence that the design and development has had the benefit of expertise from all the system fields which are involved.
For periodic technical inspections, the documentation shall describe how the current operational status of "The System" can be checked.
"The System" shall be designed to operate, under non-fault and fault conditions, in such a way that it does not induce safety critical risks.
"The System" shall respect, under non-fault and fault conditions, all the appropriate performance requirements specified elsewhere in UN R175.
"The System" shall be developed according to the development process/method declared by the manufacturer.

A description shall be provided which gives a simple explanation of all the control functions of "The System" and the methods employed to achieve the objectives, including a statement of the mechanism(s) by which control is exercised.
Any described function of "The System" that can be over-ridden shall be identified and a further description of the changed rationale of the function's operation provided.
A list of all input and sensed variables of "The System" shall be provided and the working range of these defined.
A list of all output variables which are controlled by "The System" shall be provided and an indication given, in each case, of whether the control is direct or via another vehicle system.
The range of control exercised by "The System" on each controlled output variable shall be defined.
Limits defining the boundaries of functional operation of "The System" shall be stated where appropriate to system performance.
A list shall be provided, collating all the units of "The System" and mentioning the other vehicle systems which are needed to achieve the control function in question.
An outline schematic showing the units of "The System" in combination shall be provided with both the equipment distribution and the interconnections made clear.

The function of each unit of "The System" shall be outlined and the signals linking it with other units or with other vehicle systems shall be shown, either by a labelled block diagram or other schematic, or by a description aided by such a diagram.

Each unit of "The System" shall be clearly and unambiguously identifiable (e.g. by marking for hardware and marking or software output for software content) to provide corresponding hardware and documentation association.

Where functions are combined within a single unit or within a single computer, but shown in multiple blocks in the block diagram for clarity and ease of explanation, only a single hardware identification marking shall be used.
The unit identification defining the hardware and software version shall be changed where the software changes such as to alter the function of the unit as far as this Regulation is concerned.
In case of a failure of "The System", the driver shall be warned, for example by warning signal or message display.

When "The System" is not deactivated by the driver (e.g. by turning the ignition (run) switch to "off", or by switching off that particular function if a special switch is provided for that purpose), the failure warning shall be present as long as the fault condition persists.

Where the chosen fault provision of "The System" selects the removal of the Higher Level Function, all the corresponding output control signals associated with this function shall be inhibited in such a manner as to limit the transition disturbance.

"The System" shall have measures in place to ensure that it does not prejudice the safe operation of the vehicle when its performance is affected by environmental conditions, e.g. climatic, temperature, dust ingress, water ingress, ice packing.

The reaction of the System under the influence of a failure in any individual unit shall correspond with the documented summary of the failure analysis, to a level of overall effect such that the safety concept and execution are confirmed as being adequate.
